narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that Brexit polls were reasonably accurate in depicting a close race between Remain and Leave voters, rather than being wildly inaccurate.

units.meaning: At the final time point, both Remain and Leave poll at about 46.1% (46.0750), indicating a very close race or tie at the end of the series.
accepted_routes: Final poll shows both at about 46.1%.
Last poll: Remain and Leave both around 46%.
The endpoint value is roughly 46.1% for both sides.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the final time point with both entities at approximately 46.1%.
units.temporal_anchor: the polls were actually showing a close race
units.reviewer_question: Is the final poll value (~46.1% for both) a required takeaway, or is it optional?

units.meaning: Across all provided time points, Remain and Leave have identical values (zero difference), depicting a tied or extremely close race throughout.

basis.note: same as Leave at final point
same as Remain at final point

accepted_routes: Remain and Leave are tied at every poll.
No gap between Remain and Leave at any time point.
The race is level across all provided polls.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show Remain and Leave values as equal at each time point, with no visible gap between them.
units.temporal_anchor: the polls were actually showing a close race
units.reviewer_question: Must the video convey that Remain and Leave were tied/equal at every poll, or is a general close-race statement enough?

units.meaning: The polling values range from a low of about 38.2% (38.2167 at x=715) to a high of about 46.1% (46.0750 at x=1160).
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the low point around 38.2% and the high point around 46.1%.
units.temporal_anchor: it also wasn't an instance where the polls were wildly off
units.reviewer_question: Should the full range (~38–46%) be required to show polls were not wildly off?

units.meaning: The polling values generally trend upward over the period, from about 39.3% at the first time point to about 46.1% at the last.
accepted_routes: The polls trend upward over the period.
Polling values rise from about 39% to about 46%.
The series generally increases from start to end.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show a general upward movement from the first to the last time point.
units.temporal_anchor: for most of the final month
units.reviewer_question: Is the upward trend over the period required, or optional?

units.meaning: The change from the first to the last poll is an increase of about 6.8 percentage points (46.0750 - 39.2833 = 6.7917) for both entities.
accepted_routes: The change from first to last poll is about +6.8 percentage points.
Both sides gain roughly 6.8 points from start to end.
The final value is about 6.8 points higher than the first.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the first-to-last increase of about 6.8 percentage points apparent.
units.temporal_anchor: for most of the final month
units.reviewer_question: Is the ~6.8-point increase from first to last a required derived change?

optional_valid: The first poll value is about 39.3% for both entities.
The series has minor fluctuations, such as a dip to 38.2167% at x=715.
The final month shows a narrowing or level race with no entity pulling far ahead.
unsupported_to_avoid: Leave led Remain for most of the final month (table shows identical values for both).
Betting markets suggested Remain would win (not in table).
Polls were wildly inaccurate (not in table).
Any claim that the polls predicted the exact referendum result.
Causal explanations for why the polls were close or accurate.
Remain and Leave percentages sum to 100% (not stated and not true for these table values).
notes: The table's unit is %, so absolute percentages are allowed. However, Remain and Leave rows are identical at each x, so units about a Leave lead are unsupported.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
